I can't give you the letter for q3, even in practice. Quiz 0001 is still ungraded, and a retake only tells you what you can recall if the answer stays with you. After I grade it, I'll go through q3 with you in full. If you'd like me to grade your s2 attempt, say so.

You can still work it out without me. Here's a way in that applies to every option equally.

Ask what is actually going wrong in the story. The agent isn't missing information, because all 40 steps are in its context. It also isn't stopping, because it keeps repeating itself. Then, for each option, ask what it changes about that situation.

- **Does it change what the model can see or how it's told to behave?** That changes the model's inputs.
- **Does it change the program around the model?** The question asks for a change to the agent program, and the loop is what that program runs.

Then try one more test on each option: "If the model keeps making the same edit anyway, what happens next?" Some options still leave the loop running with no end. Others guarantee it ends.

This ties to your mission. When you defend the makerspace assistant at your design review, someone will ask what stops it from burning your small model budget on a stuck request. Your answer will come from this same reasoning.

Write one or two sentences saying which kind of option you think guards against a stuck loop, and why. I'll tell you whether your reasoning holds. I won't tell you which letter it points to.
